scenes.title: The explanation fits too well
scenes.viewerPurpose: Coherence Pressure proposes a name for the pull to connect things before the evidence is there.
scenes.composition: A parent beside a family table holding a tablet (unwanted app with a removal cross) and a phone of short videos; a dashed bridge with a question mark arcs between them; the child arrives in sentence 2.
addOrChange: Keep the bridge visibly proposed; no proof tick or diagnosis label; shorten the opening record text.
Round-1 repair: no causal arrow (the link is dashed and questioned); the child named in sentence 2 appears; recognisable devices replace labelled cards; no in-art text.

cues.visualAction: Parent, brows raised and mouth relaxed, looks toward the phone and holds an open questioning hand toward the devices; only then the dashed, questioned bridge appears between them.

The parent turns to the child with a calm face and holds a palm-up inviting hand toward them; the child frowns and pushes the unwanted app away, then turns head and gaze to the phone, smiles and steps toward it, reaching for the videos.

scenes.title: Two ordinary observations
scenes.viewerPurpose: A model finds a way to connect the two through attention and choice.
scenes.composition: The parent, seated, reads the model's answer on a laptop; a bridge joins the tablet and phone under the shared words attention and choice, then opens into a questioned link.
addOrChange: Remove repetitive feed swaps and extra parent gestures; avoid making this a claim about the child’s psychology.
Round-1 repair: five salient objects; the bridge terminates on both devices; the vocabulary sits under the bridge it names; no cards, no child standing on a label.
Round-3 repair: the desk is wider than the laptop; the questioned arc uses 14 px dashes with 20 px gaps, matching scenes 1 and 3.

cues.visualAction: The seated parent, interested (raised brows, relaxed mouth), leans toward the laptop and holds a pointing/explaining hand on the model's reply through the sentence; a solid bridge joins tablet and phone and the words attention / choice appear beneath it.

The parent turns sceptical (one brow raised, other eye narrowed, flat mouth), rests her chin on her hand with the other forearm folded, and looks up at the arc as the solid bridge is replaced by the same arc dashed and broken by a question mark; the words remain.

scenes.title: A connection still to prove
scenes.viewerPurpose: The book examines how convincing connections can appear before anyone has tested them.
scenes.composition: A reader examines the dashed, questioned bridge between tablet and phone under a magnifying glass; the book arrives with its own term on a tag and the glass moves onto it.
addOrChange: Remove the settled avoidance/exploration labels, which give away analysis before the viewer reads it.
Round-1 repair: the floating arrow is gone; the magnifier is the single scrutiny device applied to both the observed connection and the book's own term.
Round-3 repair: devices sit low under a high questioned bridge so the raised pointing arm and gaze go to the lens unobstructed.

cues.visualAction: Worried reader, standing right of the low devices, raises one arm and aims an index finger up at the magnifying glass over the high, questioned bridge, eyes on the lens; the other hand opens in doubt.
The book with its question sticker appears right beside the reader; the reader turns gaze to it with a calm, attentive face and points at it while the same magnifier moves onto the book.

scenes.title: Before the story closes
scenes.viewerPurpose: For people who think and write with AI, the original conversation makes the problem easy to recognize.
scenes.composition: A reader holds the original conversation (chat bubbles) in one hand beside the polished explanation (neat lines, seal) in the other; the book lies open on a reading table.
addOrChange: Remove benchmark diagrams and multiple case outcomes; keep one comparison and a reading cue.
Round-1 repair: the arrow ending in a gap is removed; the comparison is enacted by the reader's two hands holding both pages side by side instead of an unimplemented finger cue.
Round-3 repair: warm closed smile; hands overlap page edges; the reader steps up to the reading table in sentence 2.

cues.visualAction: The reader, with a closed warm smile and softly raised brows, holds the original conversation beside the polished explanation, each page gripped at its inner edge, then looks toward the open book.

The reader settles: arms and pages lower and he steps up to the reading table (the polished page reaches its edge), gaze on the open book, a curious face, while a question mark rises between reader and book; nothing is ticked yet.

checks: Do not generate voice until all122 script and visual plans pass review.
Use only source-grounded diagrams and neutral illustrative examples; preserve uncertainty and proposal labels.
Measure audio and keep the complete film at or below120 seconds without accelerating narration.
Inspect Color, Light and Dark at desktop and phone sizes; verify captions, labels and cue timing.
Listening review and visual QA are separate from having a compiled film.

revision.reason: Independent visual review (round 2) failed expressions and gestures; arms became held, authored poses and faces were corrected by art.mjs.
